adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent`'s fallback searches `destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` using the very variable that was just proven falsy in the ternary, so the `.find` can never match a real entry and silently returns `undefined`, causing `calendar.events.update` to be called with `calendarId: undefined`/no calendarId guard downstream and potentially hitting the wrong (primary) calendar without any error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the updated `updateEvent` logic sets `selectedCalendar` via `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only case where the `: ...find(...)` branch runs), the predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy value, so it will not match any real destination calendar entry and will return `undefined`. This makes the fallback path ineffective and can lead to an undefined `selectedCalendar` being used for `calendar.events.update` (whether that errors or falls back elsewhere isn’t shown here, but the selection logic itself is demonstrably incorrect).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback for `deleteEvent` sets `calendarId` to `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (the fallback case), the `.find(...)` predicate compares against that same undefined value, so it will not select any destination calendar and returns `undefined`. This makes the fallback path effectively broken and can cause the delete to target a default calendar (likely `primary`, given `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` immediately above), rather than the intended destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — destinationCalendar was widened to an array to support multiple hosts, but every LarkCalendarService method (createEvent, createAttendees, updateEvent, deleteEvent) still only reads index 0, so for this integration the array is effectively cosmetic and multi-host support is silently unimplemented here

adjudication.rationale: The diff widens `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` and EventManager now creates events per-destination (`createAllCalendarEvents` loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calls `createEvent(...)`). However, in `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, and `deleteEvent` all destructure only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365CalendarService.createEvent destructures only the first destinationCalendar entry, meaning this integration never actually supports the multi-host destinationCalendar the type change was meant to enable, creating a mismatch between the type contract and the real behavior

However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` now always uses only the first entry via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and builds the events URL from that (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`). There is no selection by `credentialId` (unlike the updated Google integration), so when `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries, Office365 will keep targeting the first calendar regardless of which credential is being used for that create call, leading to wrong-calendar inserts or 404s.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — createAllCalendarEvents loops over destination calendars (one per collective-event host) and runs a sequential `prisma.credential.findUnique` inside the loop instead of a single batched `findMany({ id: { in: [...] } })

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents` was changed to `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and, when a matching credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } ... })` inside that loop. This creates an N+1 query pattern and runs sequentially per destination calendar instead of batching (e.g., collecting credentialIds and using a single `findMany`), which is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the diff, not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:518 — updateAllCalendarEvents iterates every calendar reference (scales with host count on collective events) and issues a sequential `prisma.credential.findUnique` per reference rather than batching with `findMany

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `updateAllCalendarEvents` was changed to collect all calendar references via `.filter(...)` and then loop them (`for (const reference of calendarReference)`). Inside that loop, when a matching credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: reference.credentialId } ... })`. Because this `findUnique` is awaited inside the loop, multiple calendar references (e.g., scaling with host count in collective/team scenarios) will trigger sequential DB round-trips rather than batching (e.g., `findMany` over all needed IDs) or parallelizing. This is a diff-grounded performance/scalability concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:428 — Cancellation loop over bookingCalendarReference (one entry per host) performs a sequential `prisma.credential.findUnique` per reference inside the loop instead of a single batched `findMany` keyed by the collected credentialIds

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts, bookingCalendarReference was changed from a single .find(...) to a .filter(...) and iterated via `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that loop, when a matching credential isn’t found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, it performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` per reference. This is verifiably sequential DB querying within the loop and could be optimized by collecting credentialIds and doing a single `findMany` (or preloading) to avoid N round-trips. This is a performance/efficiency concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:502 — In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, per-reference `updateEvent(...)` promises are pushed unawaited into `result` and resolved via a single `Promise.all(result)`; if any one host's update rejects, the whole call rejects and the catch marks every host's reference as failed, masking partial success/failure per host

adjudication.rationale: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` the diff changes `calendarReference` to an array and then builds `result` by pushing `updateEvent(...)` calls inside a `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop. The whole block is wrapped in a single `try/catch`, and the `catch` now returns failures for *all* references via `calendarReference?.map(...)`. This means if any one `updateEvent(...)` promise rejects (e.g., when later awaited/aggregated), control jumps to the `catch` and all hosts’ calendar references are reported as failed, losing partial success/failure granularity introduced by the multi-reference change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 — Lark createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent now silently pick only the first destinationCalendar entry ([mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar) with no test verifying correct behavior when multiple hosts have Lark destination calendars

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array (e.g. `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`, `packages/core/builders/CalendarEvent/class.ts`). In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent` now do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;` which always uses only the first entry. Meanwhile `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates over `event.destinationCalendar` and attempts to create events per destination/credential, but it passes the same `event` object (containing the full array) to each integration. Unlike Google, Lark is not updated to select the destination calendar by the current credential, so when multiple Lark destination calendars exist it will write/delete/update against the first calendar ID, causing incorrect calendar selection (wrong calendar or failure) rather than handling each destination correctly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — Office365 createEvent likewise only uses the first destinationCalendar entry, untested for the new multi-host array scenario

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and updates GoogleCalendarService to pick the destination calendar entry matching the current credentialId. In contrast, Office365CalendarService.createEvent now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and uses only that first entry’s `externalId` to build `eventsUrl` (Office365CalendarService.ts around line 73). In multi-destination scenarios (e.g., collective/team events where `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` adds multiple entries), this can select the wrong calendar for a given credential, potentially creating the event in the wrong calendar or failing due to permission/calendarId mismatch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts — No existing test suite (unit or integration) exists at all for EventManager despite this PR introducing a significant behavioral change (single destinationCalendar -> array, per-host credential resolution, DB credential fallback fetch); the fix ships with zero automated regression protection

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows substantial new branching/looping logic in `packages/core/EventManager.ts` (e.g., `createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `event.destinationCalendar[]`, fetches missing credentials via `prisma.credential.findUnique`, and passes `externalId` into `createEvent`; `updateCalendarEvents` now processes an array of calendar references and also falls back to DB credential fetch). In the diff, the only test-related change is a Playwright e2e expectation update (`destinationCalendar: null` -> `[]`), and no unit/integration tests are added/modified to exercise these new EventManager behaviors. While the claim that *no* EventManager tests exist at all cannot be proven from this diff alone, it is fair and specific to note that this PR introduces nontrivial behavioral changes without adding targeted automated regression coverage in the changeset.
